results.title: Hexis Review 2026: An Independent Assessment After 12 Months | Roadman Cycling
results.content:
The setup itself takes about ten minutes. The learning curve is steeper than MyFitnessPal because you need to understand why your targets change day to day. There is no hand-holding tutorial — you either grasp the concept of periodised nutrition or the daily fluctuations will feel random and confusing. This is a real barrier. I have spoken to riders who set up Hexis, saw different numbers every day, assumed the app was broken, and deleted it within a week.

It is not broken. It is doing exactly what it should. But Hexis does a poor job of explaining this to new users.

## Daily use — what it is actually like

The daily experience has two halves: the intelligent part and the tedious part. [...] Hexis has improved here. The 3.0 redesign in May 2025 overhauled the interface, and subsequent updates added voice logging, better serving size calculations, and recipe handling. The energy and macro reallocation feature — which recalculates your remaining meals when you eat more or less than planned — is smart and useful. But the core logging experience still trails behind dedicated food trackers. If you are coming from MyFitnessPal, the difference in logging speed will frustrate you for the first few weeks.

I stuck with it because the periodisation intelligence is worth the friction. Whether you will reach the same conclusion depends on how much you value the daily macro adjustments versus how much you hate slow food logging.

## What actually changed [...] The App Store rating reflects growing pains. As of July 2026, Hexis sits at 3.2 out of 5 on the UK App Store from 56 ratings. The negative reviews cluster around early reliability issues and food logging friction. The positive reviews consistently praise the periodisation intelligence and the TrainingPeaks integration. The app has improved substantially — the 3.0 redesign, Garmin integration, voice logging and macro reallocation are all meaningful additions — but the rating has not yet caught up with the current product.
